turns.prompt_text: are there color blindness glasses for dude on topic people
turns.response_html:
Yes, there are several brands that make glasses specifically for deutan (red-green) color blindness. These lenses work by filtering out overlapping light wavelengths to help your brain better distinguish between reds and greens.

Recommended Brands

  • EnChroma: The most well-known brand, offering specialized "Outdoor Deutan" and "Indoor Universal" lenses.
  • Pilestone: A more budget-friendly option with lenses categorized by the severity of your deficiency (e.g., Lens A for mild/moderate deutan).
  • Vino Optics: Uses different technology originally designed for medical use to enhance blood and oxygen visibility under the skin, which helps with red-green contrast.

Key Considerations

  • Lighting: Most of these glasses work best in bright, natural sunlight; indoor versions are usually less effective.
  • Adjustment Period: Your brain often needs 15–30 minutes of wear time to "recalibrate" to the filtered light.
  • Effectiveness: They do not "cure" color blindness or grant 100% normal vision, but they significantly improve contrast for most users.

turns.prompt_text: can they be combined with my prescription lenses or would it decrease the effectiveness
turns.response_html:
Combining color blindness technology with prescription lenses is common and generally does not decrease the effectiveness of the color filtering. In fact, many users find the experience better because the world is both color-enhanced and in focus.

Here is how you can approach combining them:

1. Prescription Color Blind Glasses (Best Integration)

Most major brands like EnChroma and Pilestone offer prescription services. You provide them with your current prescription (including your pupillary distance), and they custom-build the color-filtering technology directly into the corrective lenses.

  • Pros: Single pair of glasses; maximum clarity.
  • Cons: Most expensive option (EnChroma prescription pairs often start around $400–$600).

2. Fit-Over Glasses

These are designed to be worn directly over your existing prescription frames.

  • Pros: Most affordable way to "combine" the two; you can take them off quickly to compare views.
  • Cons: Can be bulky or heavy on your nose; might feel less stylish.

3. Clip-Ons

If you have a standard frame shape, you can buy color-blind filtering "clips" that attach to your current glasses.

  • Pros: Very lightweight and convenient.
  • Cons: May not fit all frame styles perfectly; can occasionally cause glare between the two layers of glass.

Does it decrease effectiveness?

No, but with two small caveats:

  • Lens Coatings: If your current prescription glasses have a very strong "Blue Light" filter or a specific colored tint, it could theoretically interfere slightly with the color-blind filter's precision. Standard anti-reflective coatings are perfectly fine.
  • Light Loss: Because color-blind glasses work by "filtering out" certain wavelengths of light, they naturally make the world appear a bit darker (like sunglasses). Layering two sets of lenses (as with Fit-Overs) can slightly increase this effect, though usually not enough to be an issue in daylight.

Recommendation: Since you are in the Ames/Ankeny area, you might check with local specialists like Ames Eye Care or Wolfe Eye Clinic to see if they have EnChroma samples. Trying a "Fit-Over" style in-person would let you see exactly how the filtering interacts with your specific prescription before you commit to a custom-made pair.
